thread:
sam liu: quick brain dump: thinking about a probabilistic hedging model for canary/A-B rollouts that factors capacity signals into fallback decisions. goal: smoother, capacity-aware failover with less oscillation. short thread to capture tradeoffs and who's doing what.

maya ramirez: curious 14 how is this different from our current threshold+lease approach?

sam liu: current feels too binary: route owner is either healthy or not. probabilistic hedge assigns a dynamic weight to each variant (A, B, fallback) tied to both health and capacity headroom. routing becomes sampling from the weight distribution rather than an all-or-nothing cutover.

ben okoye: hmm. sampling may add variance to user experience. how do we bound regressions?

sam liu: we clamp hedges by a max-regret budget per tenant. e.g., limit B exposure so we don't exceed a 1% regression budget for key metrics. also we can anneal weights faster/slower based on SLA classes.

zoe kim: operationally we need a compact state to sync to routers. can't push large distributions every second.

sam liu: agreed. design: each variant exposes a compact heartbeat: {epoch, weight_score, capacity_pct, p99_ms}. routers pull lightweight weights (single float) and an epoch. weight_score is computed by owner from local signals using a shared scoring function.

maya ramirez: scoring function needs to be stable across owners. want a deterministic mapping so router logic stays simple.

sam liu: plan: define canonical scoring proto in RFC (linear blend of normalized p99, errors, cpu, queue_depth) -> weight_score in [0,1]. owners can apply local caps (e.g., reserved capacity) before publishing.

ben okoye: what about fast escalations when capacity evaporates quickly (node drain, OOM)? probes might lag.

sam liu: include a reactive short-circuit: node-level drain emits a "capacity_alarm" flag. when router sees alarm from a variant it reduces that variant's effective weight multiplicatively by alarm_backoff (0.1-0.5) instantaneously. alarms are edge-triggered and gated by a cooldown window.

zoe kim: we should avoid routing loops where two variants keep nudging each other27s weights. any stability guard?

sam liu: yes: add inertia via exponential smoothing and min_stay_window per-weight update. also require a weight-change quorum from owners for cluster-wide variants.

maya ramirez: how does this play with Dedicated/Private deployments and tenancy isolation?

sam liu: per-tenant policy: hedging_mode: [none, local-only, global-capable]. default is local-only; global-capable only if tenant permits. routers consult tenant ACLs before sampling from global pools.

ben okoye: metrics and observability? this probabilistic approach needs new SLO tooling to reason about expected regret.

zoe kim: agree. we need simulation dashboards that replay historical traffic with candidate hedging params to estimate cost/regret. add sample traces for deterministic repro.

sam liu: quick config sketch for RFC: 

``nhedge_policy:
  mode: probabilistic
  scoring_proto: v1
  probe_interval: 3s
  smoothing_alpha: 0.25
  min_stay_window: 20s
  alarm_backoff: 0.2
  max_regret_pct: 1.0
  tenant_policy_default: local-only
``n
maya ramirez: rollout plan? I'd like shadow experiments in staging with traffic replay + canary stage in prod with very low weight for fallback.

sam liu: yep. propose three-phase: 1) scoring proto + router pull contract landed; 2) simulate offline + load tests; 3) staged canary: 0.5% global hedging for a week, gradually increase if no regressions.

ben okoye: cost implications: more cross-variant traffic could raise token spend. need budget-aware sampling: weight_score *= (budget_remaining / budget_threshold) clamp.

zoe kim: also tie to quota vault so routers can reject samples that would exceed reserved tokens, falling back to best-effort cached result.

maya ramirez: emergency ops control? we need a single switch to freeze hedging and pin variant weights during incidents.

sam liu: add operator API: hedging.pause(tenant) and hedging.pin(tenant, variant). must emit audit logs and be RBAC-protected.

ops-bot: hedging.feature-flag toggled to OFF for tenant: acme-corp by maya (reason: incident drill)

sam liu: volunteers: ben can own sim infra and cost modeling, zoe can spec router pull protocol and rate limits, maya will draft the RFC + rollout plan. I'll implement scoring prototype.

ben okoye: will start a Jupyter sim and load replay harness.

zoe kim: will sketch the lightweight pull proto and a minimal protobuf for weight_publish.

maya ramirez: RFC draft by EOD Friday? then sync in architecture meeting next Tue.

sam liu: thanks all. I'll add a brief sequence diagram and failure scenarios to the RFC (node drain, network partition, and quota exhaustion).
